rv.q: When all is said and sung, Blaemire (Glory Days, Space Dogs), who wrote the book, music, and lyrics, has created a mixed bag of a musical.
The experience of watching this show is engaging, and it’s packed full of metaphor and meaning while also maintaining a plot that is easy to follow.
Soon grapples with both the existential and practical side of dying. But its perspective on living rarely resonates emotionally.
The trees may be ablaze, but this is Manhattan, so groceries can still be ordered, and thus romance finds its way into Charlie’s homestead.

cn.t: Blaemire's intimate musical about a woman paralyzed by climate anxiety divides critics. Some praise its surprising psychological depth, while others find the doomsday premise muddled and the romantic comedy elements don't quite land.
